name: Chroma
subcategory: open-source vector / search database for AI (embeddings, retrieval, agent context)
origin_detail: Begun in 2022 by Jeff Huber (CEO) and co-founder Anton, initially on active learning for training data, with a May 2022 pre-seed led by Anthony Goldbloom (AIX Ventures) with James Cham (Bloomberg Beta) and Nat Friedman and Daniel Gross (AI Grant); pivoted to an embeddings database after ChatGPT; ChromaDB first released in October 2022 (repo created 2022-10-05); HQ San Francisco
openness_notes: Initial 3: ChromaDB has been Apache-2.0 since its first commit (2022-10-05) and the company sold nothing until its hosted service. Between Chroma Cloud's GA (2025-08-18) and Oct 2026 the business was a usage-priced managed service plus paid BYOC deployments, with some code kept in private repos, i.e. close to open core (2) in that period. Current 3: at the Replit deal (2026-10-23) Chroma committed additional code from its private repos to the Apache-2.0 repository, wound down Chroma Cloud (writes off 2026-12-07, reads off 2026-12-22) and stopped BYOC, leaving the product as Apache-2.0 code that Replit says it will keep contributing to. No foundation or neutral governance, so not 4. The licence never changed.

license_history.note: Single LICENSE commit, 'Initial commit' 2022-10-05; no later licence-type change

license_history.license: Apache-2.0 engine + proprietary managed service (Chroma Cloud)
license_history.note: Chroma Cloud GA 2025-08-18, 'a cloud-native, distributed implementation of Chroma', usage-based pricing; BYOC offered with a fixed minimum cost

license_history.license: Apache-2.0 (incl. code moved from private repos)

relicensing_events.outcome_note: Done as Chroma agreed to join Replit and shut Chroma Cloud, to give open-source users 'the strongest continuity story'; the exact components opened were not listed on the fetched pages

exit_events.note: 2026-10-23: Chroma 'has signed a definitive agreement to join Replit'; terms undisclosed. Replit's Amjad Masad (a seed investor) and Michele Catasta were early Chroma investors. Chroma Cloud is being wound down within 60 days; work on ChromaDB and Foundation continues at Replit

risk_events: Hosted business arrived late and was short-lived: Chroma Cloud GA 2025-08-18, wind-down announced 2026-10-23 (writes disabled 2026-12-07, reads 2026-12-22), so Cloud customers (case studies: Factory, Propel, Mintlify) must migrate
Independent database vendor absorbed by an application company (Replit) on undisclosed terms; future stewardship of the Apache-2.0 project depends on Replit
robustness: Apache-2.0 code, ~29.7k GitHub stars and 2.6k forks (Nov 2026), about 6M downloads a month (Oct 2026; the homepage cites 11-15M), used in over 90k open-source codebases; previously private code was released under Apache-2.0 at the Replit deal, so users can self-host. No foundation or neutral governance; the hosted service ends 2026-12-22.
physical_science_relevance: An embedded, local-first vector store usable for retrieval over papers, lab notebooks or instrument documentation without running a server; Apache-2.0 permits academic and commercial use, and the project survives the Cloud shutdown.
openness_effect_assessment: Openness made Chroma a default RAG vector store almost immediately (35k Python downloads in its first five weeks, ~30k stars, 90k dependent codebases) and attracted an $18M seed in Apr 2023. Adoption did not become a durable hosted business: Chroma Cloud reached GA only in Aug 2025 and was wound down 14 months later when the company joined Replit. Under that pressure Chroma did not relicense; at exit it opened previously private code.
key_takeaway: Chroma is the cautionary case for an AI-era open-source database: permissive from day one, massive developer adoption, but no disclosed revenue, no funding after the 2023 seed and an undisclosed-terms exit to Replit (an early investor) in Oct 2026, with its cloud shut down. Unlike the 2018-2024 database relicensing wave (MongoDB, Elastic, Redis), the end-game was an acqui-hire plus opening more code, not a restrictive licence.
